pr_body:
We must implements `agg_list` for `NullChunked`, otherwise it will be dispatched to the default implementation which doesn't produce a list series.


This fixes #15437.

issue_context.title: Unexpected behaviour of pl.Expr.over
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl


df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": ["a", "a", "b", "b", "b"],
        "b": [None, float("nan"), None, None, None],
        "c": [None, None, None, None, None],
    }
)

# The code snippet below works
df.with_columns(
    pl.concat_list(pl.col("b"))
    .list.eval(pl.element().cast(pl.Float64).fill_nan(None))
    .flatten()
    .drop_nulls()
    .len()
    .over("a")
)

# The code snippet below fails
df.with_columns(
    pl.concat_list(pl.col("c"))
    .list.eval(pl.element().cast(pl.Float64).fill_nan(None))
    .flatten()
    .drop_nulls()
    .len()
    .over("a")
)
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

When working with `Null `columns, we want to cast them for `f64` and, if there is any `float('nan')`, fill it with `None`. 
This behaves as expected in all cases but when the column values are all `None`. In such a case, we get a `PanicException`:

```python

PanicException: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: SchemaMismatch(ErrString("invalid series dtype: expected `List`, got `null`"))
```

This is unexpected, as when running:

```python
df.with_columns(
    pl.concat_list(pl.col("c"))
    .list.eval(pl.element().cast(pl.Float64).fill_nan(None))
    .flatten(),
    pl.concat_list(pl.col("b"))
    .list.eval(pl.element().cast(pl.Float64).fill_nan(None))
    .flatten()
)
shape: (5, 3)
┌─────┬──────┬──────┐
│ a   ┆ b    ┆ c    │
│ --- ┆ ---  ┆ ---  │
│ str ┆ f64  ┆ f64  │
╞═════╪══════╪══════╡
│ a   ┆ null ┆ null │
│ a   ┆ null ┆ null │
│ b   ┆ null ┆ null │
│ b   ┆ null ┆ null │
│ b   ┆ null ┆ null │
└─────┴──────┴──────┘
```

Columns `b` and `c` have the same type and values.

### Expected behavior

We would expect the behaviour when all the values are `None` to be the same as when one value is populated, even with `float('nan')`.

comments:
An attempt at a minimal repro:

```python
df = pl.select(a = None)

df.select(pl.concat_list("a").over(1))

# PanicException: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: 
#     SchemaMismatch(ErrString("invalid series dtype: expected `List`, got `null`"))
```

I think this is not caused by `over`. The following example can also reproduce:
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [None], "b": [1]})
df.group_by("b").agg(pl.col("a").drop_nulls())
```

I will take a look.
